object: Let t be the mean of the separately L2-normalized A1 and A2 native-factor response means, and let p be the L2-normalized P response mean. Among arbitrary real coefficient vectors w satisfying <t,w>=1 and <p,w>=0, compute the minimum Euclidean norm. This is a relaxation of factor masking, not a causal-program guarantee.
derivation: Project t into the orthogonal complement of unit p. Its norm is ||t|| sqrt(1-cos(t,p)^2). The minimum-norm feasible w is that projected vector divided by its squared norm, hence ||w||=1/(||t|| sqrt(1-cos^2)). The target-only aligned solution has norm 1/||t||.
interpretation: Even an unconstrained signed linear recombination needs about 5.24 times the coefficient norm of the target-aligned solution to cancel mean P while preserving unit target response. A binary native-factor subset is more constrained. This does not prove impossibility, but it predicts noise and construction sensitivity for pruning-only repair and favors locating a context-dependent read/write sign gate.
